cockpit.generate:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create one polished, production-plausible desktop APPLICATION COCKPIT screenshot for AdaptOps. Brand name spelled exactly A d a p t O p s. This is a new visual proposal for the existing approved Direction A, not a new visual direction. Landscape 16:10, high resolution, crisp readable English text. Flat front-facing application screen, no laptop hardware, no perspective, no decorative scene.

Visual language: premium sober enterprise decision desk, white and very pale blue-grey surfaces, deep navy typography, deep teal #086273 actions, subtle mint and amber/red status chips, hairline cool-grey borders, restrained 10px corner radii, Inter-like sans-serif, clear alignment, plenty of breathing room. No purple, no glassmorphism, no giant illustrations, no decorative gradients. Use small sharp outline icons only. A compact 64px top header and approximately 190px left navigation, central working area and narrow evidence/activity panel.

All key copy must be exact and legible. Top left "AdaptOps", next small text "Demo Materials", top right small pill "Design preview" and "Paul · Operations". Under the company name show a discreet but readable "Synthetic company data · 22 Oct 2026". Left navigation items: "Overview" selected, "Needs decision", "In progress", "Completed", "Watches", separator, "Company knowledge". No invented notification counters.

Main heading "What changes for your business" with subtitle "Market signals connected to your commitments and opportunities." Directly below, a compact company-context strip labelled "Your company context" with three simple groups "Sites & stock", "Orders & reservations", "Suppliers & customers". This company is already known. No setup wizard and no giant chat box. No fake ERP brands or logos, no connectivity claims.

The primary central card has a small amber "Mixed impact" chip and "Needs review". Title "Insulation supply: prepare a coordinated response". Subtitle "Protect committed deliveries and assess additional demand." Two clear sections inside the same card:
Left section with restrained red accent: "Risk to commitments", "Site A · 8 ISO100 pallets · due 23 Oct", "Internal delivery-date confirmation", small "Synthetic business fact" chip.
Right section with mint accent: "Opportunity to qualify", "Check demand and compatible free stock", "Existing commitments remain protected", small "More facts needed" chip.
Below both sections a very clear footer "Next step: review the response plan" and one strong teal button "Review plan →".

Below the main card, a compact two-column row:
Card 1 "Calculated response" with one large value "€1,420" and precise label "Proposed emergency purchase cost". Under it "Site A covered · Site B protected". Small secondary line "Transfer remains conditional". Do not call this a saving, revenue or realised benefit.
Card 2 "Human decision" with "Review the evidence, adjust the plan, then approve." and a subtle note "Approval and execution have separate states."

Right panel labelled "Evidence & activity". First evidence card: "Public evidence", "Collected source available", "Supplier relationship still to verify", subdued blue "Public source" chip. Second card: "Company records", "Stock, reservations and order dates", subdued slate "Synthetic ERP/CRM" chip. Then small vertically arranged activity items "Company context received", "Coverage calculated", "Awaiting review". A compact bottom link "View evidence and calculations →". Do not invent elapsed times, a real-time monitoring badge or fabricated source headline.
A small unobtrusive footer within the canvas reads "UX proposal · Risk flow evidenced; opportunity and action execution pending integration". Do not use any em dash character.

Aim for a convincing lean demo application, all main content visible in the viewport, strong hierarchy, no scrolling, no excess small text. No footer marketing website, no pitch slide, no invented charts, forecasts, financial gains or completed purchases.
